definition: Subject appears small against the location
use_case: Showcase the location so the setting becomes a character

definition: Subject is visible but shown with a lot of surrounding space
use_case: Keep the subject in view amidst grand surroundings

definition: Subject fills the frame while scenery is still emphasized
use_case: Feature multiple characters together

definition: Frames the subject from the knees up
use_case: Buffer between a full shot and a medium shot

definition: Frames the subject from mid-thighs up
use_case: Originally used to show gunslingers' holsters
example_film: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly

definition: Frames the subject from the waist up
use_case: Dialogue scenes and intimate moments

definition: Frames the subject from the chest up
use_case: Favor the face while maintaining some distance

definition: Fills the frame with the subject's face or a detail
use_case: Reveal emotions and reactions

definition: The most extreme level of detail
use_case: Emphasize a specific feature or object

definition: Wide shot revealing a scene's location
use_case: Set the geography at the start of a scene

definition: One character featured in the frame
use_case: Standard composition for a performance

definition: One featured character with background elements visible
use_case: Add context via extras or partial obstruction

definition: One character alone in the frame with nothing else
use_case: Isolated focus on a character

definition: Two characters in the same frame
use_case: Show connection, chemistry, or dynamics between characters

definition: Three characters in the frame
use_case: Efficient coverage for group scenes
example_film: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows – Part 1

definition: Subject filmed from behind another character's shoulder
use_case: Common setup for conversation scenes

definition: Subject filmed with another character's hip in the foreground
use_case: Suggest a power imbalance between characters

definition: Shows exactly what a character sees
use_case: Transport the audience into a character's perspective

definition: Focus shifts from one subject to another within the shot
use_case: Aggressive use of focus as a storytelling device

definition: Subject is in focus while foreground/background is blurred
use_case: Place emphasis squarely on the subject

definition: Everything in the frame is in sharp focus
use_case: Make the audience feel the importance of the full scenery

definition: Selective focus creating a miniature-model effect
use_case: Highly stylized, dreamlike quality

definition: Nothing in the frame is fully sharp
use_case: Dream or memory sequences

definition: Two simultaneous focal lengths within one frame
use_case: Draw attention through an unnatural, layered effect

definition: Camera positioned at the subject's eye height
use_case: Neutral perspective mimicking natural viewing

definition: Camera looks up at the subject
use_case: Emphasize power, dominance, or superiority

definition: Camera points down at the subject
use_case: Create a feeling of inferiority or vulnerability

definition: Camera positioned roughly waist-high
use_case: Varied, grounded perspective composition

definition: Camera positioned at the subject's knee height
use_case: Emphasize a character's superiority or scale

definition: Camera positioned at ground level
use_case: Capture the perspective from the floor looking up

definition: Camera positioned at shoulder height
use_case: Standard composition that maximizes a subject's presence

definition: Camera slanted to one side
use_case: Create disorientation and unease

definition: Camera shooting from directly above
use_case: Establish scale and overall movement/blocking
example_film: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind

definition: Shot captured from a helicopter or drone
use_case: Establish a large landscape or expanse

definition: No camera movement during the shot
use_case: Emphasize subject movement and performance

definition: Camera mounted on a specialized wheeled cart
use_case: Move the viewer bodily toward or away from a subject — smooth, controlled, building or releasing intimacy without a cut

definition: Lens focal length changes during the shot (no camera movement)
use_case: Alter the viewer's focus without physically moving the camera

definition: Camera position and focal length altered simultaneously in opposite directions
use_case: Make the world warp and lurch around a character at the moment of dread or realisation, while they stay the same size

definition: Camera rotates horizontally from a fixed position
use_case: Reveal new information or follow action sideways

definition: Camera rotates vertically (up/down) from a fixed position
use_case: Follow action or reveal information vertically

definition: Rapid pan that creates motion blur
use_case: Fast, energetic transition between subjects

definition: Rapid tilt that creates motion blur
use_case: Fast vertical transition between subjects

definition: Camera physically moves alongside the subject
use_case: Follow character movement fluidly

definition: Dolly moves horizontally, side to side, like a crab
use_case: Travel sideways with a subject so they hold in profile while the world slides past behind them

definition: Camera moves in a circular arc around the subject
use_case: Reveal surroundings from multiple angles around a subject

definition: Camera mounted on a three-legged stand
use_case: Static shots plus basic pans and tilts

definition: Camera rides on a short track along one axis
use_case: Keep a near-static frame quietly alive with a small, smooth, deliberate move rather than locking it off

definition: Camera held and moved directly by the operator
use_case: Add a gritty, realistic, immediate feel

definition: Camera stabilizer rig worn/carried by the operator
use_case: Glide with a moving character weightlessly and without jolts, so the viewer travels with them rather than chasing them

definition: Motorized gyroscopic stabilizer
use_case: Compact stabilization for moving through tight spaces

definition: Large arm-mounted rig that sweeps the camera over a scene
use_case: Dramatic reveals sweeping up and over a scene

definition: Smaller crane-like device with limited range
use_case: Cost-effective alternative to full crane-style shots

definition: Aerial camera mounted on an unmanned aircraft
use_case: Follow subjects from the air or establish a landscape

definition: Camera moves along a suspended cable or wire
use_case: Sweep smoothly above a crowd or across a large space on a fixed path, giving scale to an event

definition: Camera creeps steadily toward the subject across the shot
use_case: Close pressure in on someone as a thought lands, tightening the frame so the viewer leans in with them

definition: Camera withdraws steadily from the subject across the shot
use_case: Reveal how small, alone or surrounded someone is by opening the frame away from them

definition: Camera drops from a high vantage down into the scene
use_case: Drop the viewer out of the sky and land them inside a place, establishing a world then joining it

definition: Camera rises away from the subject and gains altitude
use_case: Lift away from someone to end a scene, leaving them small in a world that continues without them

definition: Operator-carried camera breathing and wandering slightly around the frame
use_case: Put the viewer inside an unstable, immediate moment that feels observed rather than staged

definition: Camera fixed rigid on sticks with no movement whatsoever
use_case: Hold absolutely still so the viewer has nowhere to look away to, making stillness or dread unbearable

definition: Focal length is yanked in or out in a single fast beat
use_case: Punch attention onto a detail abruptly, landing a joke or a shock without cutting
